meta.method: WebSearch plus WebFetch, about 50 calls. 'confirmed: true' means the figure or wording was read on the fetched page at the cited URL (through WebFetch's page summary, quoted where possible). 'confirmed: false' means it came only from a search-result snippet or a secondary page that was not fetched, or the page could not be fetched; the note says which. Nothing is estimated. Where no figure was found, the entry says 'not found'. Several primary pages failed: citizensinformation.ie and agriland.ie returned 403, gov.uk/quad-bikes-and-trikes and ontario.ca/page/off-road-vehicles-ontario-roads returned 404, Lowe's returned 403, the Tractor Supply product page timed out, the CT DMV fee page dropped the connection twice, erde.co.uk did not resolve, and the Federal Reserve 1996 model-forms PDF could not be decoded.

atv_on_road.item: New York: ATV on a highway, the general rule
atv_on_road.figure: Prohibited, with two exceptions: (1) a direct crossing of a highway other than an interstate or controlled-access highway, 'at an angle of approximately ninety degrees', after a complete stop, yielding to traffic, and at an intersection when crossing a divided highway, with lights on from half an hour after sunset to half an hour before sunrise; (2) 'any highway which has been designated and posted as open for travel by ATVs' under VTL 2405
atv_on_road.publisher: New York State Senate (NY Vehicle and Traffic Law §2403)
atv_on_road.note: The page has the crossing and designated-highway text. The full list of crossing conditions (stop, yield, divided-highway, lights) is from the Justia/Senate search snippet of the same section; the Senate page itself confirmed the 90-degree crossing and the designated-highway clause.

atv_on_road.figure: $12.50 per year, plus a $12.50 licence plate fee at first registration
'You may not operate any ATV anywhere in New York State, except on your own property, unless it is covered by liability insurance.'

atv_on_road.item: Connecticut: ATV on a public highway
atv_on_road.figure: CGS §14-387 prohibits operating an ATV on any public highway, except that, if operated by a licensed motor vehicle operator, it may cross a public highway (not a limited-access highway) at approximately 90 degrees, after a complete stop, yielding right of way, where no obstruction prevents a quick and safe crossing
atv_on_road.note: From search snippets of CGA OLR reports 2002-R-0807 and 2010-R-0442; the 2010 report failed on a TLS certificate error and chapter 255 was not fetched.

atv_on_road.figure: ATVs operated in Connecticut must be registered unless operated on property owned or leased by the ATV's owner
atv_on_road.note: Search snippet only. Registration fee not found.

atv_on_road.figure: OHVs meeting equipment requirements, driven by an operator with a valid driver's licence, may use highway sections legally designated and signed for combined use, which 'cannot be more than three miles long'; all OHVs may cross a two-lane highway at approximately 90 degrees where a quick and safe crossing can be made (CVC 38025, 38026). An off-highway vehicle 'may not be operated on a California highway even though it may be highway legal in its home state'
atv_on_road.note: The search snippet also said on-highway (street) registration is open only to dual-sport models, not ATVs; that line was not confirmed on a DMV page.

atv_on_road.figure: Green sticker for CARB-compliant OHVs; red sticker for those that do not meet CARB emission standards (with seasonal riding limits)
atv_on_road.note: Search snippet only; the fee was not found.

atv_on_road.item: Great Britain: licence for a quad on the road
atv_on_road.figure: Category B1: 'You can drive motor vehicles with 4 wheels up to 400kg unladen or 550kg if they're designed for carrying goods.'
atv_on_road.note: The page did not say explicitly that a category B (car) licence covers B1. Secondary sources (lblaw.co.uk, bikesure) say a full car licence, or a B1 licence issued before 1997, is needed, and that a motorcycle licence alone does not cover a quad.

atv_on_road.item: Great Britain: registration, tax, MOT, insurance for a road quad
atv_on_road.figure: 'All quad bikes, if they are to be used on the road must be approved, registered and taxed'; registered with the DVLA with number plates; MOT if more than three years old; 'a minimum of third party insurance'; only type-approved quads may be used on roads, or the owner can apply for approval
atv_on_road.note: A law-firm page, not GOV.UK; the GOV.UK quad page (gov.uk/quad-bikes-and-trikes) returned 404. The page's mention of a 'tax disc' is out of date (paper tax discs ended in 2014).

atv_on_road.item: Great Britain: agricultural quad on the road
atv_on_road.figure: Agricultural quads may use the road only when 'travelling less than 1.5 km between sites' for work; they need no MOT but must be registered and licensed for road use

atv_on_road.item: Ireland: quad on a public road
atv_on_road.figure: Legal on public roads if it has tax, insurance, a driving licence, Revenue registration and number plates; 16 to drive a light quad of 350 kg or less with a design speed of no more than 45 km/h, 17 for a heavier quad; since November 2023 a training course with a registered provider is compulsory for anyone driving a quad, even on a farm; a motorcycle or specialist ATV helmet is required
atv_on_road.publisher: Tralee Today (republishes Citizens Information's 'Know Your Rights' column)
atv_on_road.note: The primary page, citizensinformation.ie, returned 403. The licence category was not stated.

atv_on_road.item: Ireland: motor tax on a road quad
atv_on_road.figure: €333 a year if taxed as a general haulage tractor, otherwise taxed as a private vehicle by engine cc

atv_on_road.item: Ontario: ORV types allowed on roads
atv_on_road.figure: Single-rider ATV, two-up ATV, UTV, ROV, XTV and off-road motorcycle (ORM)
atv_on_road.note: Highway Traffic Act and O. Reg. 316/03; roads are open only where a municipal bylaw allows ORVs, or where the road is listed in O. Reg. 8/03 (snippet).

atv_on_road.figure: Driver at least 16 with at least a G2 or M2 licence; registered with a licence plate (northern exemptions); insured under a motor vehicle liability policy; driver and passengers wear an approved motorcycle helmet; ride on the shoulder (or the travelled portion if the shoulder is unsafe); 20 km/h maximum where the limit is 50 km/h or less, 50 km/h where it is over 50 km/h; passengers at least 8
From July 1, 2015, two-up ATVs, side-by-sides and UTVs were allowed on the shoulder of public roads where permitted, and helmets and seatbelts or footrests became mandatory for all riders
atv_on_road.note: From search snippets; the fetched ontario.ca page did not mention 2015.

atv_on_road.item: British Columbia: ORV on a highway
atv_on_road.figure: May cross a highway without an operation permit where the crossing is controlled by a stop sign or traffic light; may 'travel on any highway anywhere local police authorize, within the limits set out in an operation permit'; operation permit term up to two years; highway use requires ICBC Basic insurance and a valid driver's licence
atv_on_road.note: Off-Road Vehicle Act plus Motor Vehicle Act changes. A municipality may also allow access by bylaw (ATV BC, not fetched).

atv_on_road.item: British Columbia: ORV registration and permit
atv_on_road.figure: One-time combined plate and registration fee of $48; operation permits issued free by local police; 'If you operate an ORV on or across highways, you're required to obtain ICBC's Basic Insurance'; a valid driver's licence is needed for public roads, highways and forest service roads

atv_on_road.item: Mexico City: quad (cuatrimoto) on city roads
atv_on_road.figure: not found. The Reglamento de Tránsito de la Ciudad de México does not name cuatrimotos, cuadriciclos or vehículos todo terreno; Art. 21 fr. V bars motorcycles under 250 cc from the central lanes of controlled-access roads
atv_on_road.publisher: PAOT (copy of the Reglamento de Tránsito CDMX)
atv_on_road.note: Confirmed only that the regulation is silent on quads. A sales blog (sharmax.com, not fetched) says a quad cannot use urban roads without homologation and plates. On federal roads, the federal regulation (RTCPJF) bars quadricycles from controlled-access routes and allows them only on the shoulder of other federal roads (snippet, not fetched).

lease_early_termination.figure: 'the difference between the remaining balance on the lease and the amount credited for the vehicle (realized value of the vehicle)'; it may also include 'fees for disposal of the vehicle, transfer fees, and taxes', plus late charges and past-due payments; 'The charge may be up to several thousand dollars and may exceed the amount you would have paid if you had completed the lease.'
lease_early_termination.publisher: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, 'Keys to Vehicle Leasing'

lease_early_termination.figure: 'the actual wholesale price received for the vehicle or a wholesale value established by some other means, such as an independent appraisal'

lease_early_termination.item: Federal Reserve: methods for the lease balance
lease_early_termination.figure: Constant yield (actuarial) method, 'the most commonly used method', and the Rule of 78 method

lease_early_termination.item: Federal Reserve: worked example, constant yield (adjusted lease balance)
lease_early_termination.figure: Adjusted capitalized cost $18,800.00; term 48 months; base monthly payment $244.69; residual $12,350.00. Each month the balance falls by the depreciation part of the payment (payment minus rent charge): month 1 rent charge $131.39, depreciation $113.30, balance $18,686.70; month 2 depreciation $114.10, balance $18,572.60. After 24 payments the balance is $15,847.42, which is $1,024.34 lower than under the Rule of 78
lease_early_termination.note: The $131.39 rent charge figure is from the search snippet; the page summary confirmed $113.30, $18,686.70, $114.10, $18,572.60 and $15,847.42. The early termination charge is then this balance minus realized value, plus any early termination fee and other charges in the contract.

lease_early_termination.figure: Payoff $16,000 minus amount credited for the vehicle $14,000 = early termination charge $2,000
lease_early_termination.note: Search snippet only; the fetched page summary did not reproduce it.

aircraft_depreciation.item: Cessna 172 (1974 model) Vref values over time
aircraft_depreciation.note: One airframe's value over calendar years, not a curve by age, and it rose at times. The article says aircraft built in 1986 or earlier kept depreciating, while models from 1997 on had 'bounced off the bottom'. Old data.

aircraft_depreciation.figure: $15,000-$25,000 a year in the first 10 years; a $450,000 new aircraft worth $280,000-$320,000 by year 8; 55-60% of original value retained by year 12; 40-year-old 172s lose about $500-$1,000 a year
aircraft_depreciation.note: Search snippet only, not fetched; source of the numbers not stated.
